validator_existence_and_exit_code.rationale: A validator exists in the sense that @dbml/core's Compiler.interpretFile() detects syntax and referential errors, and dbml2sql does log them to stderr with file/line/column positions. But nowhere in export.ts, import.ts, index.ts, or bin/dbml2sql.js does the code call process.exit(1) or throw past the top level on a CompilerError for the export (dbml2sql) path — hasErrors is computed but only used to suppress a success message, and the process would exit 0 by default. import.ts (sql2dbml) does `return` after logging a CompilerError rather than throwing, which also does not set a non-zero exit code. To sit behind a deterministic CI gate the way factory/scripts/structurizr validate does, a wrapper script would need to grep dbml2sql's stderr output for error lines, or call the underlying @dbml/core Compiler API directly and exit non-zero itself — a workaround layered on top of the CLI, not the CLI's own documented behaviour.

svg_export.rationale: SVG export exists, but only via a third-party, independently-maintained CLI (dbml-renderer) that is not part of the official @dbml/cli toolchain and is not published as an official Docker image (see source-dbml-docker-registry.json) — using it inside an ephemeral container the way factory/scripts/structurizr does would require building a custom Dockerfile around this unofficial npm package, not pulling a maintained image.

png_export.citation: softwaretechnik-berlin/dbml-renderer README.md — no PNG output format is documented anywhere in the README's usage or output-format description
png_export.rationale: Neither @dbml/cli nor dbml-renderer documents a PNG output path. The only documented output format across both toolchains is SVG (from dbml-renderer) and SQL/DBML (from @dbml/cli). Producing PNG would require piping dbml-renderer's SVG through a separate, undocumented conversion step (e.g. an SVG rasteriser), which is outside what either project documents or ships.

GitHub issue search for 'exit code' on holistics/dbml returned no relevant open issue confirming or contradicting this (only unrelated dependency-bump PRs), so there is no maintainer statement either way; the finding rests on direct code reading alone. No PNG-export issue or feature request was found in a light search of the dbml-renderer repository, and no PNG output format appears in its README.
